children.name: Hydrolea brevistyla Verdc.
children.description: The native range of this species is W. Tanzania to Zambia. It is a annual and grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Hydrolea corymbosa J.F.Macbr. ex Elliott
children.description: Hydrolea corymbosa, commonly known as skyflower or corymb false fiddleleaf, is a species of flowering plant in the family Hydroleaceae.

children.name: Hydrolea elatior Schott
children.description: Hydrolea elatior is a species of flowering plant belonging to the family Hydroleaceae.

children.name: Hydrolea floribunda Kotschy & Peyr.
children.description: The native range of this species is W. Trop. Africa to SW. Uganda. It is a annual and grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Hydrolea macrosepala A.W.Benn.
children.description: The native range of this species is W. Trop. Africa to South Sudan. It is a annual and grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Hydrolea ovata Nutt. ex Choisy
children.description: Hydrolea ovata is a species of flowering plant known by the common names ovate false fiddleleaf and blue waterleaf.

children.name: Hydrolea palustris  Forsyth fil.
children.description: The native range of this species is W. Trop. Africa to South Sudan and Tanzania, Madagascar. It is a annual and grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Hydrolea quadrivalvis Walter
children.description: Hydrolea quadrivalvis is a species of flowering plant in the family Hydroleaceae that is known by the common name of waterpod.

children.name: Hydrolea sansibarica Gilg
children.description: The native range of this species is Tanzania (incl. Zanzibar). It is a annual and grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Hydrolea uniflora Raf.
children.description: Hydrolea uniflora, commonly known as the oneflower false fiddleleaf, is a species of flowering plant in the family Hydroleaceae.

children.name: Hydrolea zeylanica  Vahl
children.description: Note: From its annotations, it is difficult to see how 322.2 (LINN) could be accepted as original material for the name, but as no other original material appears to exist, Davenport's choice of this material as lectotype is accepted as a neotypification (under Art. 9.8).
